sources.entry: Pesty - Free and open-source clipboard manager inspired by Paste, with a slide-up color-coded strip, pinboards, and search. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/momenbasel/pesty) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]
Pesty - Free, open-source clipboard manager inspired by Paste, with a slide-up color-coded clipboard strip, pinboards, search, and keyboard-driven pasting.

summary.one_liner: Pesty is a free, open-source, native macOS clipboard manager written in Swift and SwiftUI that shows clipboard history as a slide-up, color-coded strip.
summary.what_it_does: Pesty records everything you copy and lets you bring it back with a global hotkey (default ⌘⇧V), which opens a translucent strip at the bottom of the screen. You pick a clip with the arrow keys or ⌘1–⌘9, press return, and it pastes into the app you were using. Cards are header-tinted per source app and show the app icon, type, time copied, a preview, and character count. It handles plain text, rich text, links, images, files, and colors, and supports pinboards for clips you reuse, typing to search history, and optional iCloud Drive sync. It runs as a menu-bar app and ignores clips marked concealed by password managers.
use_cases: Recover something copied earlier on a Mac
Search clipboard history for a previous snippet or link
Save reusable snippets in named pinboards
Paste clipboard items quickly with the keyboard
Replace Paste or Maccy with a free alternative
Sync clipboard history across Macs via iCloud Drive
how_to_run: Download Pesty-x.y.z.dmg from the latest release and drag Pesty to Applications
notable: Color-coded slide-up strip with per-app header tints
Pinboards for named, color-tagged collections that never expire
Zero third-party dependencies, signed and notarized
Keyboard-first: arrow keys, return to paste, ⌘1–⌘9 quick-paste, plain-text paste modifier
Mac App Store build is sandboxed and requests no permissions
caveats: Requires macOS 14+ and Xcode 16+ (Swift 6) to build from source
Direct-download and Homebrew builds ask for Accessibility permission to paste directly; the App Store build instead requires pressing ⌘V yourself
Building a signed and notarized DMG needs a Developer ID certificate and an App Store Connect API key
